items.title: HC can't grant relief if anticipatory bail plea premature: Supreme Court overturns relief to Sunil Biyani
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday set aside a Bombay High Court ruling protecting Future Group’s non-executive director Sunil Biyani from arrest in a ₹1,200-crore Goods and Services Tax (GST) scam [ Union of India v. Sunil Biyani ]. Notably, the High Court had granted this protection even though it held that Biyani's anticipatory bail application in the matter was premature, since the GST authorities had not passed any order under Section 69 (power to arrest) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act. In its February ruling, the High Court had directed that if any such order for Biyani's arrest is issued by the GST authorities, he should not be arrested for a week from the date of intimation of such order. The Central government challenged this ruling before the Supreme Court. It questioned whether High Courts possess inherent jurisdiction to grant interim protection from arrest to a litigant after holding that their anticipatory bail petition is premature and unmaintainable. A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu today ruled that the manner in which protection from arrest was given by the High Court was impermissible. "We have set aside the direction contained in para 6 (giving interim protection for a week from the date on which any future arrest order maybe passed), saying that it is not permissible in law," said the Bench. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu However, the Court cautioned that the GST authorities must communicate arrest orders clearly, so that anyone facing apprehensions of arrest in GST cases can ascertain which legal remedies they would want to avail. "But to ensure that anyone facing apprehension of arrest is not placed in a position of irreparable damage, section 69 order has to be communicated. And in terms of the rules framed under CGST act every dealer has to provide his email address. So therefore the notice can be communicated to their email address. Appeal stands disposed of on the aforesaid terms," the top court said. A detailed copy of the judgment is awaited. The matter arose from a summons issued by the Directorate General of GST Intelligence (DGGI) to Future Group’s non-executive director Sunil Biyani. The underlying probe pertained to a large-scale fake invoicing and circular input tax credit racket with a total GST implication of over ₹200 crores. items.title: Russia appoints former CJI DY Chandrachud as arbitrator in dispute with Ukrainian bank
items.summary: Former Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud has been appointed by Russia as its arbitrator in an investment treaty dispute brought by Ukrainian state-owned bank Oschadbank. According to a report by Global Arbitration Review , Costa Rican arbitrator and former trade minister Dyalá Jiménez will preside over the three-member tribunal. Jiménez was jointly selected as president by both sides. The third arbitrator will be Greek arbitrator and National University of Singapore professor Stavros Brekoulakis who was appointed by Oschadbank. The arbitration has been initiated under the 1998 bilateral investment treaty between Ukraine and Russia. Oschadbank’s claim concerns assets and operations in the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions that it claims it lost following Russia’s military actions in Ukraine, particularly after the full-scale invasion in 2022. The claim is understood to be worth hundreds of millions of dollars. Oschadbank initiated the proceedings after a notice of dispute served on Russia in July 2025 allegedly went unanswered. Justice Chandrachud had previously declined approaches from Russia to serve as its arbitrator in treaty claims brought by Wintershall Dea and Ukrenergo. The approaches were reportedly made on the same day that the Permanent Court of Arbitration designated him as the appointing authority in the Wintershall proceedings. He later stepped down from that role after disclosing the communications. Oschadbank is represented by Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan partners Epaminontas Triantafilou and Alex Gerbi, along with Asters partners Oleksiy Didkovskiy, Andrii Pozhidayev and Oksana Legka. Russia is represented by Pinna Goldberg partner Andrea Pinna, counsel Pratyush Panjwani and senior associate Dimitrios Papageorgiou.

items.title: US court accepts Trump government proposal to dismiss fraud charges against Gautam Adani but terms it "highly unusual"
items.summary: A United States court has dismissed securities and wire fraud charges against Indian industrialist and billionaire Gautam Adani and two other executives, bringing the criminal proceedings against them to an end. Judge Nicholas G Garaufis of the US District Court for the Eastern District of New York on August 11 accepted the proposal of the US Department of Justice (DOJ) to dismiss all three charges brought against Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and Vneet Jaain - securities fraud conspiracy, wire fraud conspiracy and securities fraud. However, Judge Garaufis expressed concern about the manner in which the DOJ made the proposal and termed it "highly unusual". " The fact that McCotter came to this decision largely in collaboration with defense counsel, and seemingly without input from the FBI and SEC agents who investigated the alleged misconduct, or the attorneys from the Department, SEC, and U.S. Attorney’s Office who brought the case, appears to be highly unusual, " the order said. The Court's decision to drop charges comes after multiple affidavits were filed by Adani and DOJ over two months. Since Adani was not charged with either conspiracy under Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) or obstruction of justice, no criminal charge under this indictment remains pending against him. The Court, however, reserved its decision on DOJ’s request to dismiss the FCPA conspiracy charge against Ranjit Gupta, Cyril Cabanes, Saurabh Agarwal, Deepak Malhotra and Rupesh Agarwal, as well as the obstruction charge against all of them except Gupta. These counts remain open for now because the Department has not adequately supported its reasons for seeking their dismissal. According to prosecutors, bribes worth ₹2,029 crore, or about $265 million, were promised to officials of State electricity distribution companies. items.title: Tamil Nadu: Engineering student beaten to death; five students held
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A 19-year-old engineering student in Coimbatore was allegedly beaten to death by a group of his college mates on Monday, August 10, following allegations that he was involved in an extortion and mobile phone theft incident. Five students have been detained in connection with the death. The deceased, K Amuthan, was a native of Kallakurichi district, studying at Hindustan Engineering College in Coimbatore. According to reports, Amuthan had recently been suspended from the college hostel after allegedly assaulting a cook employed there. He was subsequently staying with friends in a rented room near Othakkalmandapam. On Monday morning, around 5.30 am, a group of masked youths allegedly entered a rented house in Poonga Nagar, where Elavarasan, 18, a second-year civil engineering student at the same college, was staying with his friends. The group allegedly threatened the occupants with a knife, assaulted them and fled after taking two mobile phones. During the incident, Elavarasan and his friends reportedly identified Amuthan as one of the attackers. Elavarasan subsequently lodged a complaint with the Chettipalayam police, following which a case was registered. Around 8.30 am, Amuthan and his friend Sriman, 19, were allegedly intercepted by a group of students near Malmichampatti. The group reportedly identified Amuthan as one of those involved in the earlier incident and took the two students to a ground behind the college. Amuthan was allegedly assaulted there with logs and iron rods. He managed to return to his room around 10 am. However, he developed severe breathing difficulties around 3 pm and was taken to a nearby hospital, where he died while undergoing treatment. Based on Sriman's complaint, the Chettipalayam police registered a murder case. Five college students were detained on Tuesday for questioning, while efforts are underway to identify and trace others allegedly involved in the assault. While the preliminary investigation has revealed that Amuthan was attacked in retaliation for the earlier assault and mobile phone snatching incident, Amuthan's father, Kennedy, alleges that the group attacked his son for allegedly exposing the supply of ganja in the hostel premises. He claims that information provided by his son was leaked, eventually leading to the attack. items.title: AP junior doctors to stop non-emergency services over pending stipend hike
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Andhra Pradesh Junior Doctors Association (AP JUDA) will discontinue non-emergency services in government medical colleges on Wednesday, August 12, in protest against the Telugu Desam Party (TDP)-led state government. The announcement was made late on Monday, August 11, night after a meeting with the state Health Department. The JUDA said its representatives had met the Andhra Pradesh Director of Medical Education (DME) and other officials to discuss their demands. However, the talks reportedly failed to yield a solution, prompting the doctors to continue their protest. The AP JUDA has been protesting for the implementation of Government Order (GO) 287, issued in 2009. The GO allows for a biannual stipend revision of 15% in view of inflation. The protesters argue that the periodic enhancement of the stipend paid to postgraduate students and interns has been due for more than seven months. The AP JUDA has also demanded that the biannual stipend hike be increased from 15% to 30%, citing rising inflation and workload. The government has instead proposed an annual hike of 3% for postgraduate students and 5% for interns. The Federation of All India Medical Association (FAIMA) has extended its support to the AP JUDA. items.title: Karnataka schools likely to stay open on Aug 13 as KAMS withdraws bandh closure call
items.summary: Schools across Karnataka are likely to remain open on Thursday, August 13, with the Karnataka Associated Managements of Schools (KAMS) withdrawing its earlier call for school closures. The KAMS had initially called for a closure of schools, as part of a bandh, over the ongoing Cauvery water dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The KAMS said the decision was taken because another closure would further affect academic schedules, particularly in aided schools already facing a shortage of teachers. KAMS said it would nevertheless extend moral and peaceful support to the bandh called by Kannada organisations to protest Karnataka's release of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu. School managements, teaching staff and non-teaching employees have been asked to wear black ribbons or black strips as a symbolic gesture, without disrupting classes. The association said academic activities had already been affected because teachers have been deputed for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Government-aided schools, which are dealing with an acute shortage of teachers, would be particularly affected if schools were shut again, it said. However, KAMS has left the final decision on declaring a holiday to individual school managements, particularly in view of the Karnataka government's fresh direction to release Cauvery water. Schools have been advised to consider the local situation and take a decision based on safety and practical considerations. KAMS has also suggested that schools use the day to help students understand the Cauvery dispute rather than involve them in the bandh. Students from Classes 5 to 12 could be given factual and age-appropriate information about the dispute during the morning assembly or a classroom session, the association said. The discussions could cover the history and background of the Cauvery dispute, Karnataka's dependence on the river for drinking water, agriculture and livelihoods, and the difficulties caused by inadequate rainfall and water scarcity. Students could also be taught about constitutional processes, court decisions, cooperation between states and peaceful democratic expression, as well as responsible water conservation and sustainable management of water resources.
